hypotheses.construction_plan: Define a two-argument kernel T(a,b). The members are obtained by substituting the ordered pair (i,j) into the kernel, and by substituting the permuted ordered pair (j,i) into the same kernel.
required_assumptions: T is defined on ordered pairs; no symmetry of T is assumed.
hypotheses.rationale: Both subexpressions use the same function symbol T with the same two declared symbols in reversed argument positions, indicating a common two-place kernel under a permutation of arguments.

hypotheses.construction_plan: Start from a two-variable template T(a,b)+T(b,a). Substitute (a,b)=(i,j) to obtain the full expression; the individual summands are the two evaluations of T under the identity and the transposition of arguments.
required_assumptions: Addition is commutative so the full expression is invariant under swapping i and j.
hypotheses.rationale: The raw expression is exactly a sum of the two swapped evaluations of a common two-variable function, which is the canonical symmetrization template under the transposition of the two declared symbols.
